data.title: HTTP Methods
data.tagline: The verb in a request stating which kind of operation it performs: read, create, update, or delete
data.learningOutcome: Seeing a request in developer tools, you can say what kind of operation it performs.
data.description: In the Network panel, GET /api/articles/7 and POST /api/articles are different requests. GET means safe reading; POST asks the target resource to process the request, and whether it creates or saves depends on the API contract. A method states request semantics; choosing the wrong one does not guarantee a 405 response.

learning.assumes: You have seen GET and POST, or request records in the Network panel.
learning.outcome: Seeing a request in developer tools, you can say what kind of operation it performs.

distinctions.label: Status code
distinctions.explanation: The method states the intended operation; the status code states the response result. A resource can return 405 when a method is disallowed, but a wrong method can also produce another response.

distinctions.label: Route
distinctions.explanation: A route is the URL path identifying which resource; a method is the verb stating what to do to it.

explanation.title: GET is read
explanation.text: Address-bar Enter and ordinary links are GET; it is designed to be safely resent and should have no side effects.

explanation.title: POST submits a request for processing
explanation.text: Forms commonly use POST, but POST does not inherently mean save or create; check the API contract for the operation it triggers.

explanation.title: PUT / DELETE update and remove
explanation.text: Express modification and deletion per the API contract; some APIs use POST uniformly for compatibility—follow the API docs.

data.boundary: A 405 response says the resource does not allow that method; it does not prove whether data changed. A method error may produce another status, so compare the response with the API contract.

lessonPractice.title: A delete button sends a GET request, and refreshing the page deletes again. What is the problem?

options.label: Delete should use DELETE or an agreed POST; GET is read-only semantics and can be resent
options.feedback: Correct. GET is for safe reading and may be safely retried; an operation that changes resource state should not be triggered by GET.

options.label: A frontend confirmation dialog is enough
options.feedback: A dialog cannot stop refresh, back, or retry; the method semantics are the root cause.

options.label: Change the returned status code to 404 so it won't delete again
options.feedback: A status code only describes the result; changing it does not change that GET gets resent.

data.agentPrompt: The delete button currently sends a GET request, and refresh deletes again. Change it to the semantically correct method (DELETE or the API's agreed POST) and confirm refreshing does not re-trigger it. Verify the method and result in the Network panel afterward.
